rationales: Protease digests proteins and is not the main enzyme in saliva.
Amylase in saliva begins the digestion of starch.
Lipase digests fats and is not the main enzyme in saliva.
Pepsin digests proteins in the stomach.
Guttation is the loss of liquid water through leaf pores, not evaporation.
Translocation is the movement of sugars through a plant.
Transportation is a general term for movement of substances within a plant.
Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a plant’s surface.
Albumin is a blood plasma protein but is not the main clotting protein.
Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin during blood clotting.
Antibodies help defend the body against pathogens.
Hormones act as chemical messengers rather than blood-clotting proteins.
Lipids are treated as macromolecules in this classification.
Proteins are macromolecules.
Glucose is a small molecule and is an example of a micromolecule.
Starch is a large carbohydrate polymer and is a macromolecule.
Classes are groups of related orders, not families.
Orders are groups of related families, not families themselves.
Species are grouped into genera, while a family contains related genera.
A family is a group of related genera.
Al-Baqara is not the Surah cited for the description of animal groups used to illustrate classification.
Al-Noor describes animals by how they move, illustrating their grouping into categories.
Al-Quraysh does not contain the cited description of animal groups.
Yasin is not the Surah cited for the animal-group description.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation, rather than the result of discussion and reasoning about related findings.
A law describes a consistently observed relationship or pattern.
A theory is formulated through discussion and reasoning about evidence and related hypotheses.
Data are collected observations or measurements, not something formulated by reasoning.
Margulis and Schwartz proposed a later modification of the five-kingdom scheme.
Tournefort is known for early work on plant classification, not the five-kingdom system.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom system.
Golgi bodies do not have their own DNA.
Mitochondria contain their own DNA.
Ribosomes are not DNA-containing organelles.
Vacuoles do not have their own DNA.
Amoeba commonly reproduces by binary fission.
Paramecium commonly reproduces by binary fission.
Sea stars can reproduce in other ways, but budding is not the usual example.
Hydra reproduces asexually by budding.
Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Meiosis is a type of cell division that produces haploid cells.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
Interphase is the period between cell divisions.
A coenzyme is an organic cofactor that is usually loosely bound to an enzyme.
An apoenzyme is the protein portion of an enzyme without its cofactor.
Cofactors is the general term for non-protein components needed by some enzymes.
A tightly bound organic cofactor is called a prosthetic group.
An amino acid is a building block of proteins, not ATP.
ATP is a nucleotide made of a nitrogenous base, sugar, and phosphate groups.
A fatty acid is a component of many lipids, not ATP.
A nucleic acid is a polymer of nucleotides, whereas ATP is one nucleotide.
Lipase digests fats and is not the principal stomach enzyme.
Trypsin works mainly in the small intestine.
Pepsin is a stomach enzyme that digests proteins.
Amylase digests starch and is not the principal stomach enzyme.
Albumin is a plasma protein but does not form the clotting mesh.
Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin during blood clotting.
Globulins have several roles, including immunity, but are not the main clotting protein.
Haemoglobin transports oxygen in red blood cells.
